A1.justification: Both complete 26-page PDFs describe the same MuRating work. Text comparison and rendering of every page, including Appendices 6–10, establish that the research content matches without comparison-limiting gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original 1.2B and 7B pretraining experiments, benchmark results in Tables 1–2 and 6–19, and rater, translation-quality and alignment analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains the original pretraining experiments, benchmark outcomes, ablations and appendix analyses reported in v2.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains identical English-rater aggregation, translation-based preference transfer, cross-lingual and parallel-pair training, BGE-M3 architecture and scoring procedures.

E1.justification: The English and 17-target-language corpora, benchmark tasks, 13-language comparison subset and 7B MultiLoKo evaluation are unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices 7–9.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within every reported experiment. Tables 1–2 and 6–8 retain Uniform, QuRater, AskLLM, DCLM, FineWeb-Edu, QuRater-M, HPLT-2, FineWeb-2 and FineWeb2-HQ in their respective settings.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendices 7–8 retain the same model sizes, token budgets, sampling procedures, preprocessing, metrics and few-shot evaluation settings.

E4.justification: The alignment ablations, pairwise-versus-pointwise comparison, translation-quality studies, Qwen-versus-GPT-4o robustness analysis, domain analyses and multilingual case studies are all retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Repeated-scoring descriptions and statistical displays are identical, including the 20-evaluation averages in Section 4.3.2 and Figure 5 and the translation-quality error bars in Figure 6.

E6.justification: All numerical entries, plotted results and qualitative findings match. For example, MuRater(E)'s 18-language average remains 50.96 in Table 1, and MuRater's English average remains 51.23 in Table 2; appendix results also match.

T1.justification: The preference definitions, Bradley–Terry formulation, translation-preservation assumptions and parallel-pair regularization in Section 3, including Equations 1–4, are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about unified English-rater aggregation, multilingual transfer, pretraining gains and pairwise scoring robustness.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and applicability limits are unchanged, including translation-quality explanations and limitations concerning language coverage, GPT-4o biases and narrative or creative content.

D1.justification: Appendices 6–8 retain identical prompts, hyperparameters, tokenizer details, hardware, runtime and data-processing information. Code and data resource link targets are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, research-positioning passages and all 70 reference entries are unchanged; no cited work or relationship to prior research is added or removed.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v2, dated 30 Dec 2025, to v3, dated 5 Mar 2026. PDF author metadata adds Trevor Cohn, already visible in both author lists. Prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–16, Tables 1–20, captions and page layouts are unchanged. Rendered pages 2–26 are identical; page 1 differs only in the arXiv version/date stamp.

improvement.justification: v3 preserves the scientific content, experimental evidence, interpretations, reproducibility information and appendices unchanged. The version/date stamp and PDF metadata updates do not meaningfully alter the paper's scientific quality, clarity or evidential support.
